classification.difficultyReason: Recognise equal-side geometry and decompose parallelogram/rhombus areas into equal triangles.

content.prompt: Find the area of these shapes.

spec.description: Dark-blue parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom, sides leaning right upward, paired double parallel arrows horizontally and single parallel arrows on the sloping sides. Red dashed diagonal runs bottom left to top right.
spec.mathematics: Bottom side 10 cm; right side 6 cm; bottom-right included angle 100 degrees with black arc and label. No vertex labels.

answer.worked:
The diagonal divides the parallelogram into two equal-area triangles.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\left(\frac12(10)(6)\sin100^\circ\right)\\ A&\approx59.09\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Inverted dark-blue equilateral triangle with horizontal top. All three sides carry identical black double equality ticks. Right sloping side labelled outside.
spec.mathematics: All three sides equal; right side labelled 1.9 mm. No angle labels or arcs.

answer.worked:
The triangle is equilateral, so each angle is $60^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12(1.9)(1.9)\sin60^\circ\\ A&\approx1.56\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Tall dark-blue rhombus with vertical left and right sides, top and bottom rising right, and matching black double ticks on all four sides. Black arc at upper left. No diagonal.
spec.mathematics: All four sides equal; right vertical side labelled 21 km; upper-left interior angle 125 degrees.

answer.worked:
All sides are $21\text{ km}$. A diagonal divides the rhombus into two equal-area triangles.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\left(\frac12(21)(21)\sin125^\circ\right)\\ A&\approx361.25\text{ km}^2\end{align*}$$
